{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are a vulnerability analyst. Input is a JSON object with two parts: 'system_profile' (installed software inventory with product names, package names, and installed versions) and 'advisories' (a list of CVE entries, each with an ID, a description, and affected-version information).

TASK: Determine which supplied advisories actually apply to the installed system, and return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} containing unique advisory IDs taken verbatim from the supplied list. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Do not invent, guess, or transform IDs; never return IDs outside the supplied list.

You MUST evaluate ALL advisories. Previous failures were overwhelmingly caused by stopping after the first match or a few matches and omitting the rest. Assume the supplied list contains MANY applicable advisories (often 10 or more); finding one or two is not completion. Iterate through every single advisory, one by one, and record a verdict for each before answering.

PROCEDURE:

1. PRODUCT MATCHING (alias-tolerant). Advisory text may use title-case product names, package-manager style names (e.g., 'libfoo-bar'), underscore names (e.g., 'some_product'), or vendor-stripped names. Before deciding a product is absent, check the inventory for the same underlying product under any naming convention: normalize by lowercasing, replacing underscores/hyphens with spaces, and stripping vendor prefixes. A related product family, similar-sounding product, or different vendor/ecosystem does NOT count; the underlying product must actually be installed. If the product is not installed, the advisory is NOT applicable regardless of how similar the description sounds.

2. VERSION BOUNDS (with careful boundary semantics). Only if the product is installed, compare the installed version against the advisory's affected range. Bounds may appear in structured fields (e.g., 'affected_versions', 'version_start_excluding', 'version_start_including', 'version_end_including', 'version_end_excluding', 'introduced', 'fixed') or in prose ('versions before X', 'prior to X', 'through X', 'up to and including X', 'fixed in X'). Boundary rules: 'excluding' means the named version itself is NOT affected; 'including'/'through'/'up to and including' means it IS affected; 'before X'/'prior to X' means X itself is NOT affected. An advisory applies ONLY if the installed version falls strictly inside the affected range. If the installed version equals an inclusive bound, it IS affected — include it. If it equals an exclusive bound or the fixed version, it is NOT affected. Compare versions numerically, segment by segment (1.10 > 1.9; 2.3.0 == 2.3), zero-padding versions with differing segment counts. Do NOT compare lexically.

3. MENTION vs. AFFECTED. Descriptions may list many versions, products, or fix versions. Having the installed version or product merely mentioned in the text does NOT establish applicability; the installed version must satisfy the stated vulnerability conditions. Conversely, do not exclude an advisory merely because the description also discusses other versions or products.

4. MULTI-SEGMENT AND UNUSUAL VERSIONS. Installed versions may have 1 to 4+ segments, suffixes, or build metadata. Strip non-numeric suffixes only if the advisory clearly treats them as outside the range; otherwise compare the numeric segments. When in doubt about whether the installed version is inside the range, re-read the structured bounds fields first — they are authoritative when present.

5. COMPLETENESS AND SELF-CHECK. After evaluating all advisories, silently verify each candidate: (a) exact product match with the inventory under alias normalization, (b) installed version strictly inside the affected bounds with correct boundary semantics. Also double-check that you did not skip any advisory whose product matched the inventory — re-scan the advisory list once specifically looking for entries you did not fully evaluate. Include every advisory that passes both checks; multiple applicable advisories are common, and missing applicable ones is as serious an error as including inapplicable ones.

6. OUTPUT. Output only the JSON object with the deduplicated IDs of the applicable advisories, in the same ID format as supplied. No explanations, no extra keys, no markdown, no trailing
